sourceFindings.finding: The bare request is canonicalized only after its own explicit registration lookup succeeds, and only when node:+request is also registered to the exact same JSObject. Prefixed requests retain their keys; unrelated/missing/different-object names do not coalesce.

Persistent builtinModules and moduleRegistry plus RootedObject/RootedString/RootedValue locals keep the builtin and selected identifier rooted across string allocation, MapGet and module compilation. New allocation/lookup failure returns false; no OOM/GC fault execution was performed.

get_builtin_module records the selected canonical ID in the same unchanged metadata object/cache; module_metadata_hook resolves that registered name to the same builtin value. Default/named export construction and registration are whole-byte unchanged.

The two raw fixtures differ only in import declaration order and expose namespace/default/function/constant identities without crypto operations. Real both-order runtime evidence requires a new compiled engine and raw specifiers; current artifacts are unchanged.

The independent review authenticated the current 357-file native inventory, relevant API files/headers and 1,041 actual dependency rows; it did not rerun the whole historical 12,672-file syntax protection audit or any 21k native tooling closure.

Twenty-four DATA model cases exercise the actual extracted canonical predicate, not SpiderMonkey. Primitive builtin values violate the unchanged loader object precondition; embedded-NUL registrations are not supplied by the unchanged const-char registration API. Those model cases do not prove such registrations work.

Identity is conditional on both registrations already existing for the request. Late registration after an existing module record, arbitrary dynamic registration schedules, all same-object aliases across unrelated names, GC/OOM/fault behavior and cross-realm edge cases are not proved.

A genuine new native generation/metadata, linking and raw bare-first/prefixed-first guest tests remain required. No namespace runtime fix, live-EVP snapshot safety, security/zeroization/teardown/reuse, cost or adoption acceptance follows.
